children: The US generated 1.29 billion ethanol (D6) blending credits in August, about the same as in July, according to Environmental Protection Agency data released on Thursday.
Biodiesel blending credits (D4) fell to 693 million, from 796 million in July, the data showed.

The credits, known as Renewable Identification Numbers (RINs), are used by refiners to comply with the Renewable Fuel Standard, which requires renewable fuels such as ethanol and bio-based diesel to be blended into the fuel supply. Every gallon of biofuel produced generates RINs and those who do not generate enough credits must buy them in the open market.
